items.title: Broadcom patches a VMware vCenter zero-day exploited since September
items.summary: Broadcom fixed CVE-2026-123890, an authentication bypass in the vCenter Directory Service, on 19 Nov in VMSA-2026-0009. Mandiant says a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group, Armory Castle, has exploited it since early September after first breaking in through BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances. Broadcom lists no official workaround.
items.why: Nothing to patch on ordinary WordPress hosting, but it is the kind of flaw a hosting provider running VMware would need to fix; you can ask yours if they are exposed.

items.title: Google will require Android developer verification worldwide from January 2027
items.summary: Google says the requirement will roll out in all regions in January 2027. It began blocking installation of unregistered apps in some countries this autumn, and urges developers who have not registered to do so soon.
items.why: If you or clients distribute Android apps outside Google Play, developer registration will be needed; otherwise nothing to do.

items.title: Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm third-party breaches claimed by an extortion gang
items.summary: Visa says its claim relates to a third-party service provider in Asia Pacific and that no payment data was affected. Mastercard says a provider exposed a limited number of email addresses from cardholders in one benefit program. JPMorgan Chase confirmed on social media that it is investigating a cyberattack.
items.why: Expect phishing aimed at cardholders; worth warning clients who handle payments.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.329 warns where a folder's hooks are declared
items.summary: Released on 19 Nov, version 2.1.329 adds a trust dialog warning that says where a folder's hooks are declared. It also lists scheduled tasks, /loop wakeups and forks in /tasks, and shows the JSON-RPC error message of a remote MCP server that refuses a connection in /mcp.
items.why: The hook warning is useful when you open a client repository you did not write; the /mcp error row helps debug WordPress MCP connections.

items.title: WordPress 7.2 lets abilities declare required capabilities
items.summary: A core developer note published on 19 Nov says the Abilities API in WordPress 7.2 gains a required_capabilities argument, checked with current_user_can() before every call, alongside more predictable input handling and JSON output. Input-dependent checks stay in permission_callback.
items.why: If you register abilities for Claude to use on client sites, declare the capability there instead of writing it into each permission callback.

items.title: ACF 6.8.12 adds a Settings page and turns the Abilities API on by default
items.summary: ACF 6.8.12, published on 19 Nov, adds an ACF Settings page and enables the Abilities API site-wide, including for every existing field group, post type and taxonomy. Field groups still need Show in REST API turned on for AI tools to read or update their fields. Settings already set in code stay locked.
items.why: After updating, client sites expose ACF structures to AI tools without you opting in; to keep that off, disable the setting or add the acf/settings/show_settings filter on client sites.

items.title: Perfmatters 2.7.1 fixes Cloudflare cache purges and cache warmer issues
items.summary: Released on 19 Nov, 2.7.1 fixes Cloudflare single-URL purges not invalidating edge HTML, and a sync on a shared zone that deleted another site's rules. The cache warmer now uses a plain Perfmatters/Warmer user agent, to avoid Cloudflare 520 errors on hosts such as SiteGround.
items.why: If you tried the Cache (BETA) tab from 2.7.0 behind Cloudflare, update before relying on it.

actions.title: Update every client site to WordPress 7.1.5
actions.detail: The release fixes 20 security issues, including an unauthenticated flaw that could lead to remote code execution.

actions.title: Ask hosts to update PHP to 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 or 8.2.36
actions.detail: Until then, turn off FastCGI connection reuse where it is on.
